name: North Couloir

pitch_detail.notes: Sustained snow climb (~1,200 ft) up the north-face couloir from the Honeycomb Glacier; firm corn in the morning, softening through the day.
Short rock pitch from the top of the couloir/NW Ridge directly to the summit.

descent_text: From the summit, reverse the short 5.4 pitch back to the top of the couloir. Ski parties descend the couloir itself (firm corn snow in the morning softening through the day); climbers on foot downclimb the ~1,200-ft, up-to-35-degree snow to the Honeycomb Glacier and retrace the approach.
approach: From the White River Trailhead (see Southeast Route access), reach the upper Whitechuck/Suiattle Glacier basin via the PCT and cross to the Honeycomb Glacier, or descend the Honeycomb Glacier northward from a high camp on Kololo Peaks (8,220 ft) further west along the Glacier Peak massif. Traverse the glacier to the col just west of Tenpeak and the base of the north couloir.
overview: A prominent snow/ski couloir splitting Tenpeak's north face, reached by traversing in from the Honeycomb Glacier; a sustained ~35-degree, roughly 1,200-ft snow climb finishes with one short 5.4 rock pitch to the summit via the NW Ridge.
beta: Approach via the Honeycomb Glacier — either descending from a high camp on Kololo Peaks or traversing in from the White River side over the PCT/Whitechuck and Suiattle Glaciers — to a col west of Tenpeak, then cross onto the Honeycomb Glacier and traverse to the couloir's base. Climb the roughly 1,200-ft, up-to-35-degree couloir (crampons and ice axe, or ski crampons for splitboard/ski parties), then scramble to the NW Ridge where one 5.4 rock pitch leads to the summit.
gear: glacier travel/crevasse rescue kit if approaching via glacier
